architecture.goal: Remediate the final behavioral and documentation gaps by preserving distributed daily dispatch, replacing the queue-to-workflow bridge with an ordered synchronous path, tightening retry semantics, preserving real provider failure evidence, and making dispatch-slot metadata productive instead of test-only.
runtime_shape: EventBridge Scheduler continues invoking Producer Lambda across 288 dispatch slots.
Producer Lambda continues querying one dispatch-slot partition and publishing one FIFO message per work item with MessageGroupId bound to provider identity.
EventBridge Pipe consumes the SQS FIFO queue directly and invokes the Step Functions workflow synchronously so the message remains in-flight until the workflow closes.
The Step Functions workflow is converted to Express workflow type and remains the owner of idempotency, lifecycle transitions, retries, and final persistence.
Consumer Lambda remains the business execution boundary for the provider API call, but now throws structured classified errors whose cause payload can be parsed by the workflow.
Pending-record writers become the authoritative producers of dispatchSlot, dispatchSlotPk, and dispatchSortKey during productive record creation.
A root-level ARCHITECTURE.md explains the final architecture, decisions, and traceability to challenge requirements.
explicit_non_goals: Changing the producer queue message contract beyond what is needed for Pipe input compatibility.
Changing business payload semantics sent to providers.
Adding operator UI, replay tooling, or production observability dashboards.
Manual shuffle-sharding beyond the existing FIFO High Throughput posture.
Rewriting the distributed slot scheduling model introduced in phase 3.
operational_constraints: The pipe uses an ordered FIFO source and must process one work item at a time per message group.
The pipe invokes Step Functions with REQUEST_RESPONSE semantics, which requires an Express workflow.
The pipe execution budget is finite, so one queue message maps to one workflow input and one provider execution path.
The queue message body must remain small enough for Step Functions payload limits after Pipe transformation.

module_boundaries.responsibility: Keep slot-based query and FIFO enqueue behavior unchanged, including MessageGroupId and deduplication id ownership.
Replace Orchestrator Lambda as the queue consumer and synchronously bridge one FIFO message into one Step Functions execution while preserving ordered source semantics.
Own the complete operational lifecycle for one work item, including retry classification, error normalization, persistence, and final success/failure closure.
Execute the provider API call and emit either a success payload or a classified structured error without writing persistence state.
Materialize dispatch-slot routing metadata as part of productive record creation or persistence.
Expose the final system diagram, rationale, and requirement-to-solution mapping for reviewers.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: QueueMessageContract
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Logical work-item payload published by Producer Lambda and consumed through EventBridge Pipe.
interfaces_and_contracts.compatibility_rule: This message shape remains unchanged from phase 3. The Pipe transforms transport envelope data into the workflow input without changing producer behavior.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: PipeToWorkflowInput
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Canonical workflow input built by EventBridge Pipe for one queue message.
interfaces_and_contracts.note: TTL values are injected through pipe input transformation or a preparatory workflow step rather than by a Lambda orchestrator.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: ConsumerSuccessResult
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Successful provider outcome returned from the consumer task.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: ConsumerFailureCause
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Structured error payload that the workflow can parse after catch.
interfaces_and_contracts.serialization_rule: The consumer error cause must be serializable as JSON text so Step Functions can parse it with States.StringToJson on $.workflowError.Cause.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: PendingRecordDispatchMetadata
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Routing metadata required by phase-3 slot-based dispatch and now owned by productive writes.

pending_records_write_pattern: Any productive writer that creates a pending work item must compute dispatch metadata before persisting the item.
The routing algorithm remains stable-hash modulo slots per day using recordId + providerId + scheduledDate.
Writers persist dispatchDate, dispatchSlot, dispatchSlotPk, and dispatchSortKey on the base pending-record item.
Existing test seeds remain valid but no longer represent the only source of dispatch metadata.
pending_records_read_pattern: Producer Lambda continues querying dispatch-slot-index by dispatchSlotPk for one date-slot partition at a time.
No runtime scan or enrichment job is introduced for slot metadata.
results_persistence_rule: Success paths continue persisting the exact provider status code returned in the success payload.
Terminal and exhausted transient failure paths persist the real provider status code extracted from parsed error cause payload.
Synthetic placeholders such as fixed 400 or 504 are forbidden when the real provider status code is available.
idempotency_rule: The existing idempotency table remains the authoritative duplicate guard.
Duplicate or already-claimed work still closes without writing a new final result row.

pipe_configuration.ordering_model: FIFO message group ordering preserved by ordered source semantics
pipe_configuration.retry_posture: Pipe-level retries rely on source visibility timeout and source redrive policy rather than replacing workflow business retries.

workflow_refactor.new_bridge: EventBridge Pipe invoking Express workflow synchronously
why: Preserve same-provider serialization until the workflow actually finishes.
Remove the queue acknowledgement gap created by asynchronous StartExecution.
Reduce one custom runtime hop and move transport concerns into native AWS infrastructure.

workflow_bootstrap.strategy: Introduce an initial state or transformation path that derives workflow TTL values without requiring the removed Orchestrator Lambda.
allowed_shapes: Pipe input transformer injects precomputed TTL-like strings only if supported cleanly.
Otherwise, an initial workflow step computes operational timestamps before idempotency and persistence tasks.
workflow_bootstrap.default_choice: The workflow itself computes missing TTL metadata in an initial normalization step if Pipe transformation cannot do it without brittle time math.

state_machine_definition.context_preservation_rule: The workflow root keeps workItem and workflow metadata intact throughout execution. Consumer success output is stored under a dedicated result node and caught failures are normalized under a dedicated error node.

required_states_or_responsibilities.name: NormalizeWorkflowInput
required_states_or_responsibilities.responsibility: Ensure TTL strings and transport metadata are present after Pipe delivery and before operational tasks.

required_states_or_responsibilities.name: AcquireIdempotencyLock
required_states_or_responsibilities.responsibility: Claim the logical work item before business execution.

required_states_or_responsibilities.name: MarkPendingInProgress
required_states_or_responsibilities.responsibility: Advance pending lifecycle from PENDING to IN_PROGRESS.

required_states_or_responsibilities.name: InvokeConsumerLambda
required_states_or_responsibilities.responsibility: Execute the provider API call using workItem only.

required_states_or_responsibilities.name: NormalizeWorkflowError
required_states_or_responsibilities.responsibility: Parse workflowError.Cause with States.StringToJson and project a stable error payload for persistence.

required_states_or_responsibilities.name: PersistSuccessResult
required_states_or_responsibilities.responsibility: Persist successful final outcome to tapi-results.

required_states_or_responsibilities.name: PersistTerminalFailureResult
required_states_or_responsibilities.responsibility: Persist terminal failure outcome using parsed real provider status code.

required_states_or_responsibilities.name: PersistExhaustedTransientFailure
required_states_or_responsibilities.responsibility: Persist exhausted transient failure outcome using parsed real provider status code.

required_states_or_responsibilities.name: MarkIdempotencyCompletedOrFailed
required_states_or_responsibilities.responsibility: Close idempotency record consistently for final paths.

required_states_or_responsibilities.name: MarkPendingCompletedOrFailed
required_states_or_responsibilities.responsibility: Close pending record lifecycle consistently for final paths.

required_states_or_responsibilities.name: DuplicateWorkItem
required_states_or_responsibilities.responsibility: Finish duplicate or no-longer-claimable work as a no-op completion.

result_persistence_requirements: Persisted failure rows must include providerId, recordId, processedAt, ttl, category, and parsed statusCode.
The responseBody or error payload persisted in DynamoDB must be DynamoDB-friendly and stable enough for audit.
Success path and failure paths must leave enough evidence to diagnose the exact provider response category.

classification_rule: HTTP 400, 401, 403, 404, 422, and similar business/request failures remain terminal.
Unexpected generic errors are still wrapped as transient unless a stronger classification signal is introduced.
throwing_rule: When the provider adapter classifies a failure, the thrown error must include the real provider statusCode.
The serialized cause payload must contain both the real statusCode and the human-readable message.
The error name remains the routing signal for Step Functions retry/catch logic.

required_sections: High-level summary of the final runtime architecture.
Mermaid diagram from Scheduler to Producer to SQS FIFO to EventBridge Pipe to Step Functions Express to Consumer and DynamoDB tables.
Decision rationale for replacing Orchestrator Lambda with EventBridge Pipe.
Decision rationale for precise retry/catch handling and structured failure persistence.
Decision rationale for productive dispatch-slot materialization at pending-record creation time.
Traceability matrix mapping challenge requirements to solution behaviors and repository evidence.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: A same-provider message is available while the previous one is still executing
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: The FIFO ordered source and synchronous Pipe target invocation keep the next message blocked until the prior workflow completes.
The workflow skips retries, parses the real error payload, persists terminal evidence, and closes lifecycle state as FAILED.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: A transient provider error occurs repeatedly
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: The workflow retries with exponential backoff and full jitter, then persists exhausted transient evidence with the real provider status code if retries are exhausted.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: The error payload cannot be parsed as JSON
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Fallback normalization stores the raw cause string and marks the statusCode as unavailable only when the real code truly cannot be recovered.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: A new pending record is inserted without dispatch metadata
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Forbidden by design after remediation. Productive writers must always materialize slot metadata.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: The workflow exceeds the practical execution budget of the Pipe/Express path
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: The implementation must reduce per-item execution time or timeout settings before rollout; the remediation does not support long-running per-item workflows.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Use EventBridge Pipe as the direct SQS consumer and remove Orchestrator Lambda from runtime.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: This eliminates the asynchronous acknowledgement gap that allowed same-provider concurrency leakage.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Convert the workflow to Express type.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: Synchronous Pipe invocation into Step Functions requires REQUEST_RESPONSE, which is available for Express workflows.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Keep Consumer Lambda as pure business execution without direct DynamoDB writes.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: The workflow remains the operational owner of persistence and retry semantics.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Keep slot routing algorithm stable and move its ownership to productive writes.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: This preserves the defendable phase-3 access pattern without a new enrichment subsystem.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Add root-level architecture documentation instead of scattering final rationale across phase docs only.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: The challenge is evaluated on architectural clarity, not only on code presence.

quality_gates: CDK synth reflects EventBridge Pipe, Express workflow type, and removal of the SQS-consuming Orchestrator Lambda from runtime.
Unit tests prove retry semantics no longer include States.TaskFailed.
Unit tests prove failure persistence uses parsed dynamic provider status codes.
Unit tests prove productive pending-record writes materialize dispatch-slot metadata.
Documentation deliverable exists and maps requirements to solution decisions.
expected_test_scenarios: CDK template contains an AWS::Pipes::Pipe from the provider FIFO queue to the consumer state machine with REQUEST_RESPONSE semantics.
CDK template defines the workflow as EXPRESS and preserves CloudWatch logging.
State machine definition retries TransientApiError and States.Timeout only.
State machine definition catches TerminalApiError directly into terminal persistence path.
Consumer adapter or use case serializes real provider status codes into error cause payloads.
Terminal persistence path stores 401/403/404 exactly when those provider failures occur.
Exhausted transient persistence path stores 429/502/503 exactly when those provider failures are exhausted.
Pending-record writer computes dispatchSlotPk and dispatchSortKey deterministically for new items.
Producer tests remain green for MessageGroupId, deduplication id, and slot-partition querying behavior.

phased_implementation_plan.goal: Replace the asynchronous Orchestrator Lambda bridge with an ordered synchronous native bridge.
tasks: Remove the SQS event source mapping and runtime dependency on Orchestrator Lambda.
Add EventBridge Pipe configuration in CDK from FIFO queue to Step Functions.
Convert the workflow to Express type and preserve logging configuration.
Normalize the workflow input shape so the removed orchestrator does not leave missing metadata.
definition_of_done: No runtime queue consumer lambda remains between SQS FIFO and Step Functions.
Same-provider ordered source messages remain blocked until workflow completion.

phased_implementation_plan.goal: Correct retry specificity and persist accurate provider failure evidence.
tasks: Tighten retry policy to transient errors only.
Add workflow error normalization for parsed JSON causes.
Update terminal and exhausted persistence states to use dynamic parsed status codes.
Update consumer error construction to preserve the real provider status code.
definition_of_done: Persisted failure results preserve the real provider status code.

phased_implementation_plan.goal: Make dispatch-slot metadata part of the productive data model rather than test-only data.
tasks: Identify or introduce the productive pending-record writer boundary.
Compute dispatchSlot, dispatchSlotPk, and dispatchSortKey at write time.
Add tests proving deterministic slot materialization for newly created items.
definition_of_done: New pending records are immediately compatible with phase-3 distributed dispatch.

assumptions: One queue message continues to represent exactly one logical provider work item.
Per-item workflow duration can stay within the operational limits of the Pipe plus Express workflow path.
The repository either already has or will accept a productive pending-record write boundary where dispatch metadata can be computed.
Backward compatibility with old seed-only routing data is not required beyond keeping existing tests and docs coherent.
